text: A song. A psalm of Asaph.
O God, do not keep quiet; do not be silent, do not be still, O God.

versions.text: God, do not keep silent; do not hold back, do not stay still, O God.
versions.explanation: The three verbs form a rising triad of silence/inaction; 'do not hold back' shifts תֶּחֱרַשׁ (be deaf/silent) away from the imagery of speech, blurring the poetic parallelism. Opening with 'O God' also strengthens the oral rhythm and matches the closing vocative.

text: See how your enemies are in an uproar, how those who hate you lift their heads.
Against your people they lay crafty plans; they conspire against those you treasure.
They say, "Come, let us wipe them out as a nation, so that the name of Israel is remembered no more."
With one mind they scheme together; against you they make a covenant—
the tents of Edom and the Ishmaelites, Moab and the Hagrites,
Gebal, Ammon, and Amalek, Philistia with the people of Tyre.
Even Assyria has joined them; they have become an arm of strength for the sons of Lot. Selah

versions.text: Even Assyria has joined them, lending its strength to the sons of Lot. Selah
versions.explanation: The Hebrew verb הָיוּ is plural, referring to the whole coalition, not to Assyria alone. The current rendering makes Assyria the sole subject and softens the vivid image of the 'arm' (strength) supporting Lot's descendants.

text: Do to them as you did to Midian, as to Sisera and Jabin at the brook Kishon,
who were destroyed at En-dor and became dung on the ground.
Make their nobles like Oreb and Zeeb, all their princes like Zebah and Zalmunna,
who said, "Let us take the pastures of God for our own possession."
My God, make them like whirling dust, like chaff before the wind.
As fire burns through a forest, as flames set the mountains ablaze,
so pursue them with your tempest and terrify them with your storm.
Cover their faces with shame, that they may seek your name, O LORD.
Let them be disgraced and dismayed forever; let them perish in humiliation.
Then they will know that you alone, whose name is the LORD, are the Most High over all the earth.
